subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should every public operator `cron run` be non-consuming across success, error, skipped, trigger-evaluation, retry, alert, and scheduling state, while only timer and gateway watcher executions own those transitions?
rationale: The reported deletion is clearly a bug, but the branch deliberately broadens the correction into a durable semantic contract for every operator outcome; code and tests cannot establish that public product policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Treat public manual runs as verification executions that record their outcome but never own scheduler deletion, counters, alerts, backoff, timing, or enabled state.

options.title: Narrow the fix
options.body: Prevent manual one-shot deletion while retaining selected existing counter, alert, or scheduling mutations, with explicit rules and focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Require an explicit execution mode
options.body: Preserve current behavior by default and add a separately approved operator option for non-consuming verification runs.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Treat public manual runs as verification executions that record their outcome but never own scheduler deletion, counters, alerts, backoff, timing, or enabled state.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history owns the relevant manual-run anchors, restart behavior, retry, alert, and timer scheduling semantics.
